output.headline: Approves revised 2024-25 Measure G1 allocations of up to $12.2M for schools and teacher salaries
output.summary: The Board is approving a revised resolution on Measure G1 spending for 2024-25, as recommended by the Measure G1 oversight commission. It covers allocations for named schools and for teacher salaries at OUSD and charter schools. The amount is not to exceed $12,151,876.

output.headline: Pays Digital Design Communications up to $60,000 for door openers and card readers at Oakland International

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $60,000.00

output.summary: The district is hiring Digital Design Communications, an Oakland company, to install two Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) door operator systems and a keypad card reader, with patching and painting, at Oakland International High School. Work starts March 28, 2024 and is due by April 30, 2024.

output.headline: Pays Tulum Innovative Engineering up to $59,688 to upgrade electrical wiring in two Oakland High classrooms
output.summary: The district is hiring Tulum Innovative Engineering of Oakland to build and upgrade the electrical system in classrooms 203 and 204 of the Career Technical Education building at Oakland High School. The contract is for no more than $59,688.00, paid from a Career Technical Education Incentive Grant. Work is expected to run from March 28 to May 31, 2024.

output.headline: Pays ACC Environmental Consultants up to $3,484 for a hazardous materials survey at Community Day School
output.summary: The district is paying ACC Environmental Consultants, an Oakland company, to do a limited hazardous materials survey before a planned interior demolition project at the Community Day School. The work runs from March 28 to June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Adds $300,000 to Lozano Smith's legal contract for facilities and construction work

money.evidence: in an additional not-to-exceed amount of $300,000.00

output.summary: The district is adding $300,000 to its agreement with the law firm Lozano Smith for legal services on facilities and construction matters, raising the limit from $800,000 to $1,100,000. The agreement is a memorandum of understanding (MOU) and engagement policy. The time period is unchanged at July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Directs staff to issue Proposition 39 facilities final offers to Aurum Middle and East Bay Innovation Academy
output.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution that directs staff to issue written final facilities offers under Proposition 39 for the 2024-25 school year. The offers are for Aurum Middle School and East Bay Innovation Academy. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $75,000 for Study Smart Tutors to give Burckhalter Elementary students math tutoring
output.summary: Study Smart Tutors of Westlake Village will provide tutoring during the school day, after school and on Saturdays to identified K-5 students at Burckhalter Elementary School. The goal is to improve grade-level math skills before the school year ends. The contract runs February 1 to May 23, 2024, for no more than $75,000.00, and it began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $58,630.87 for One on One Learning Corp tutoring and teacher training
output.summary: One on One Learning Corp of Miami will provide small-group and one-on-one reading, English and math help for students, training and coaching for teachers, materials for English learners, and training on digital citizenship. The work is paid from several federal Title grants and runs February 15 to June 14, 2024, for no more than $58,630.87. The agreement began before this vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $80,000 for East Bay Agency for Children staff training and counseling at Frick
output.summary: East Bay Agency for Children of Oakland will provide professional development and social-emotional counseling for staff at Frick United Academy of Language. The contract is for no more than $80,000.00, paid from the Measure G1 parcel tax, and covers August 7, 2023 to June 30, 2024. The agreement period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $41,050.44 for American Indian Child Resource Center after-school and summer programs
output.summary: The American Indian Child Resource Center of Oakland will run after-school and summer services, including tutoring, enrichment, youth development, sports, nutrition and cultural activities. The service contract is for no more than $41,050.44 and runs February 16 to June 30, 2024. A separate data-sharing agreement sets the rules for how the district shares student information with the center and how the center protects it.

output.headline: Adds $14,945 for Instruction Partners to coach Horace Mann Elementary on math and school leadership
output.summary: This amendment gives Instruction Partners of Nashville more time working with the administrator at Horace Mann Elementary School on math curriculum, instructional leadership, teacher observation and feedback. It raises the contract limit from $15,000.00 to $29,945.00. The dates stay September 14, 2023 to June 7, 2024, and work began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost summer golf and social skills program from First Tee Oakland
output.summary: First Tee Oakland, with a summer lead agency staff member, will work with 20 students at three to four school sites in summer 2024. Students will play golf and learn social-emotional skills one day a week. The program runs May 28 to July 5, 2024, at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $59,572 for International Rescue Committee human trafficking prevention training
output.summary: The International Rescue Committee of Oakland is one of the approved nonprofit partners in a human trafficking prevention grant. It will help district staff develop curriculum, train trainers, provide instruction, and advise on the district's human trafficking school safety protocol. The contract runs October 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024, for no more than $59,572.00, and began before this vote.

output.headline: Adds $10,000 to Collective Agency's contract for grant writing on a federal health funding bid
output.summary: This amendment doubles the contract with Collective Agency, LLC of Oakland from $10,000.00 to $20,000.00. The firm is writing a grant application for a federal Centers for Disease Control and Prevention funding opportunity. The dates stay July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for Youth Transportation Organization to arrange summer field trip buses
output.summary: Youth Transportation Organization of San Rafael will coordinate transportation for 300 to 400 field trips for 7,000 to 9,000 students in the 2024 summer learning programs. The contract is for no more than $50,000.00 and runs January 30 to June 30, 2024. It began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $8,000 for a consultant on human trafficking awareness and newcomer outreach
output.summary: An individual contractor in Oakland will help district staff and partners develop curriculum, train trainers, and create outreach materials for newcomer students and their caregivers. The contractor will also advise on the district's human trafficking school safety protocol. The contract runs January 22 to June 30, 2024, for no more than $8,000.00, and began before this vote.

output.headline: Adds $16,500 for Black Cultural Zone mobile murals at Bunche High after-school program
output.summary: This amendment adds money for The Black Cultural Zone Community Development to coordinate up to three mobile mural installations at Ralph J. Bunche High School during the after-school program. It raises the contract limit from $70,000.00 to $86,500.00. The dates stay July 26, 2023 to May 23, 2024.

vendor.name: The Black Cultural Zone Community Development

output.headline: Pays Care Solace up to $102,291 to connect students and families with mental health care
output.summary: The district is paying Care Solace, Inc. for a web-based service that helps staff, students and family contacts find and connect with mental health treatment providers, including a "Warm Hand-off" process. A separate data sharing agreement (DSA) covers the student information shared with the vendor. Both run from July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024, and the work began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $60,000 for Bay Area Community Resources student support at Rudsdale High
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources of San Rafael will provide counseling, case management, mentoring and referrals to students and families at Rudsdale Continuation High School, with a focus on newcomer students affected by safety concerns. The contract is for no more than $60,000.00, paid from Measure H and Measure N funds, and runs January 23 to June 30, 2024. The period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $5,100 for Growing Together garden lessons at Bunche Academy
output.summary: Growing Together - Bay Area of Pinole will work with teachers in the Hospitality, Tourism and Recreation career pathway at Ralph J. Bunche Academy to offer project-based learning centered on gardening. The contract is for no more than $5,100.00 and runs February 28 to May 22, 2024. It began before this vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $30,000 for Bay Area Community Resources site staff manager at MLK/Lafayette
output.summary: Bay Area Community Resources of San Rafael will provide a Community Staff Manager at MLK/Lafayette Elementary School. The manager will connect the school to resources, write grants, build partnerships, work with parents to boost attendance, and run Student Success Team meetings with teachers. The contract is for no more than $30,000.00 and runs February 20 to June 7, 2024. It began before this vote.

output.headline: Adds $3,000 for Luna Dance Institute weekly dance program at Kaiser Child Development Center
output.summary: This amendment adds money to the contract with Luna Dance Institute of Berkeley for a weekly 45-minute dance program for all classes, with a teaching artist working with teachers. The artist also joins monthly staff meetings and helps plan spring family events. The contract limit rises from $25,000.00 to $28,000.00, with dates unchanged (August 14, 2023 to May 24, 2024).

output.headline: Ratifies up to $2,000 for an attendance liaison at Edna Brewer Middle School
output.summary: An individual contractor in Oakland will serve as an Attendance Liaison at Edna Brewer Middle School. The liaison will call and meet with families to reduce tardiness and absences, explain attendance rules, and help recognize good attendance. The contract is for no more than $2,000.00 and runs March 1 to May 23, 2024, and it began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost Museum of the African Diaspora art program for Sankofa United 3rd and 4th graders
output.summary: The Museum of the African Diaspora of San Francisco will lead six to eight in-classroom art lessons for 3rd and 4th graders at Sankofa United Elementary School and teach during two museum field trips. The museum provides the art materials. The agreement runs February 8 to May 22, 2024, at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Approves up to $42,128.69 for Street Academy Foundation career internships at Emiliano Zapata
output.summary: Street Academy Foundation of Oakland will help students at Emiliano Zapata Street Academy take courses and do internships in the Education, Child Development and Family Services career pathway. The contract is for no more than $42,128.69, paid from Measure H and Measure N funds, and covers July 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024. The period began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $12,000 for Excel Consulting to help MLK/Lafayette principal on communication
output.summary: Excel Consulting Services, LLC of Richmond will support the principal at MLK/Lafayette Elementary School in improving communication practices to reduce complaints. The contract is for no more than $12,000.00 and runs October 23, 2023 to June 7, 2024. It began before this vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $8,653.71 for Oakland Public Education Fund mental health clinician at Think College Now
output.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund will provide a mental health clinician at Think College Now Elementary School for weekly one-on-one and small-group counseling for students. The clinician will also consult with families and staff and keep session records. The contract is for no more than $8,653.71 and runs March 1 to May 31, 2024.

output.headline: Approves Talent department Personnel Report No. 2324-0007
output.summary: The Board is asked to approve a routine personnel report from the Talent/Human Resources Department. The official text does not list individual actions or dollar amounts, so the details are in the attached report.

output.headline: Approves up to $4,233 for Oakland Public Education Fund poetry and dance workshops at Westlake
output.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund will bring local performing artists to Westlake Middle School for 15 spoken word poetry and dance workshops over four weeks, plus student performances during Black History Month. It will also train teachers remotely. The contract is for no more than $4,233.00 and runs January 22 to February 19, 2024, so it began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $25,000 for Attitudinal Healing Connection arts lessons at West Oakland Middle
output.summary: Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc. of Oakland will provide arts instruction at West Oakland Middle School that teaches students about sustainability and cultural heritage. The contract is for no more than $25,000.00, paid from the Measure G parcel tax, and runs February 14 to June 28, 2024. It began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $6,829.90 for Bay Area Video Coalition after-school media class at Skyline High
output.summary: Bay Area Video Coalition of San Francisco will provide a program manager and instructors for an after-school class called Club Real Stories at Skyline High School. The contract is for no more than $6,829.90 and runs January 8 to June 28, 2024. It began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $15,000 for Attitudinal Healing Connection after-school mural class at Bret Harte
output.summary: Attitudinal Healing Connection, Inc. of Oakland will run The After School Mural Project at Bret Harte Middle School, an advanced class where students help design and paint murals. The contract is for no more than $15,000.00, paid from the Measure G1 parcel tax, and runs January 29 to May 31, 2024. It began before this vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $5,000 for Oakland Kids First attendance challenges at Castlemont High
output.summary: Oakland Kids First will run attendance challenges and activities at Castlemont High School, where students sign attendance contracts and receive an incentive for taking part. The contract is for no more than $5,000.00 and covers December 1 to 31, 2023, a period that ended before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies a no-cost Oakland Ballet class program for 3rd graders at Oakland Academy of Knowledge
output.summary: Oakland Ballet will teach 45-minute ballet classes every Monday and Wednesday for 3rd grade classes at Oakland Academy of Knowledge, using dance to build creativity, problem-solving and teamwork. The agreement runs March 1 to May 17, 2024, at no cost to the district. It began before this vote.

output.headline: Approves up to $30,000 for Hope Reimagined mental health therapy at Sojourner Truth
output.summary: Hope Reimagined of Oakland will provide about 15 hours a week of clinical mental health services, including individual or group therapy for up to 10 sessions a week, at Sojourner Truth Independent Study. It will also provide consultation and one to three staff training sessions. The contract is for no more than $30,000.00 and runs February 15 to May 31, 2024. It began before this vote.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $22,750 for Ball for Life Oakland recess and PE coaching at Reach Academy
output.summary: Ball for Life Oakland, LLC will provide coaches to supervise and run recess games and to support physical education three days a week at Reach Academy, plus a program manager to train coaches. The company will also gather student feedback and adjust the program. The contract is for no more than $22,750.00 and runs February 1 to May 24, 2024. It began before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Hope Reimagined up to $14,700 to train educators to lead white affinity spaces

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $14,700.00

output.summary: The district is paying Hope Reimagined, an Oakland organization, to train a group of educators who identify as white to learn skills and curriculum for leading white affinity spaces. The work runs through the Office of Equity from March 4 to April 4, 2024. This is a ratification, so the agreement began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Accepts free arts visits, museum trips and teacher workshops from the Museum of the African Diaspora
output.summary: The Museum of the African Diaspora will give students at Markham Elementary School two in-class visits from teaching artists, two museum field trips and four more classroom visits focused on making artwork. It will also offer free workshops for participating teachers. There is no cost to the district, and the agreement runs from February 1, 2024 to May 29, 2026. This is a ratification, so the agreement began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Pays a contractor up to $45,000 for technology and auditorium support at Castlemont High

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $45,000.00

output.summary: The district is paying an individual contractor to maintain computers and projectors, train staff on equipment, and run lighting, sound and auditorium setup for school events and music and drama performances at Castlemont High School. The work runs from February 14 to June 30, 2024. This is a ratification, so the work began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Center for Transformative Teacher Training up to $5,000 for classroom management course

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00

output.summary: The district is paying the Center for Transformative Teacher Training, based in San Francisco, to provide its professional development course on classroom management for teachers at Lockwood STEAM Academy. The course covers a four-step model for building relationships and engaging students. The agreement runs from August 7, 2023 to August 30, 2024. This is a ratification, so the work began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Pays Rigorous Love up to $40,000 for staff and student circle training at LIFE Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $40,000.00

output.summary: The district is paying Rigorous Love, an Oakland organization, to train staff at LIFE Academy in community-building circles and mediation, and to help address staff conflict. The agreement also covers one-on-one caseload work with students and training for student leaders. The work runs from March 25 to May 31, 2024.

output.headline: Pays Kristi Yamaguchi's Always Dream up to $8,100 for a tablet reading program at Franklin Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $8,100.00

output.summary: The district is paying Kristi Yamaguchi's Always Dream, based in Danville, for a tablet-based reading program for kindergarten students at Franklin Elementary School. The program helps students learn letters, letter sounds, blending sounds, building words and sight words. The work runs from February 1 to May 20, 2024. This is a ratification, so the work began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Pays East Bay Art Therapy up to $5,000 for 24 after-school group art therapy classes

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00

output.summary: The district is paying East Bay Art Therapy, an Oakland organization, to teach 24 group art therapy classes during after-school enrichment. Groups of up to 10 students, with and without disabilities, will meet for 6 to 8 weeks each, and the provider brings all materials. The work, arranged through the Special Education Department, runs from April 1 to June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Accepts up to $41,799 from the state for an adult digital literacy and broadband project
output.summary: The Board is accepting a grant of up to $41,799 from the California Public Utilities Commission's California Advanced Services Fund (CASF) Broadband Adoption Account. The money supports the Oakland Adult and Career Education Digital Literacy Instruction Project and broadband access. The grant period is May 1, 2024 to May 30, 2026.

output.headline: Issues an official notice that North Oakland Community Charter School breached its agreement
output.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution that gives North Oakland Community Charter School an official notice of a material breach of its agreement with the district. That agreement was entered into on January 8, 2020 and amended on December 9, 2020. The text does not describe the details of the breach.

output.headline: Accepts a $25,000 Yours Humanly grant for family literacy kits at three elementary schools
schools: Martin Luther King, Jr Elementary School
output.summary: The Board is accepting a $25,000 grant from Yours Humanly, based in Walnut Creek, to pay for Family Literacy Kits (LitKits). The kits support early literacy and give children in need access to educational resources, serving more than 500 TK-2nd grade students at three elementary schools. The grant period is January 1 to June 30, 2024.

output.headline: Accepts a $264,156 Kenneth Rainin Foundation grant for K-2 literacy coaching and training
output.summary: The Board is accepting a $264,156 grant from the Kenneth Rainin Foundation for K-2 coaching and training in structured literacy. The agreement also directs $376,219 in carryover money from an earlier Rainin award to the same work. The grant period is January 1 to August 31, 2024.

output.headline: Pays National Student Clearinghouse up to $14,280 to verify graduates' enrollment and degrees

money.evidence: at a cost not to exceed $14,280.00

output.summary: The district is paying the National Student Clearinghouse for enrollment and degree verification services for district graduates. A separate data sharing agreement (DSA) sets the rules for how student data is shared with and protected by the Clearinghouse. Both run from January 1, 2024 to June 30, 2027. The work began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Accepts free TRIO college-prep programs from Mills College at Northeastern University
output.summary: Mills College at Northeastern University will provide its TRIO programs (METS and Upward Bound) to OUSD students at no cost to the district. The programs serve first-generation, low-income youth with pre-college services such as academic advising, college planning, tutoring, courses and college tours. The agreement runs from October 1, 2023 to September 30, 2024 and began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Pays The Teaching Well up to $27,740 for teacher workshops and coaching at Fruitvale Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $27,740.00

output.summary: The district is paying The Teaching Well, an Oakland organization, to provide professional development workshops and coaching for Fruitvale Elementary School, as described in an exhibit to the agreement. The work runs from November 15, 2023 to May 22, 2024 and began before the Board's vote.

output.headline: Approves a $18.9M two-year plan for arts, music and instructional materials grant funds
output.summary: The Board is approving the district's expenditure plan for the state Arts, Music, and Instructional Materials Discretionary Block Grant (Assembly Bill 181). The plan is $9,604,700 for 2024-25 and $9,315,972 for 2025-26, a grant total of $18,920,672. This is the second reading of the item.

output.headline: Ratifies the minutes of the March 13, 2024 Board of Education regular meeting
output.summary: The Board is approving the written minutes of its regular meeting held on March 13, 2024. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting.

output.headline: Amends the Board bylaw to add pay and elective course credit for Student Directors
output.summary: The Board is amending Board Bylaw 9150 on Student Directors to add compensation and elective course credit for the students who serve on the Board. The text does not state a compensation amount.
